sections.evaluation_comments:
9/17/2026
Dog did not eat.
9/9/2026
Dog was closed to back half of kennel during AM cleaning.  Slowly came forward with head lowered, ears pinned back & whale eyed.  Opened kennel door to present leash, dog would attempt to push out of gate.  Able to quickly use large loop leash.  Walked with a strong pull on leash to main PY while keeping tail tucked under body.  Would attempt to fence fight @ back half of "D" building, able to use leash to guide dog away from making contact of kennel gates as dog would continue to growl with curled lips.  Once in main PY, dog would do a shake off of body then explore with tail slightly tucked under body, sniffing nose to ground.  Would not be interested in treats or toys.  Would start to pace then stand @ corner of PY gate, flagged tail while raising hackles & low growling towards nearby kennels of "C" building.  Handler would clap hands to help get attention of dog, dog would look towards handler & continue to pace along fence line while keeping tail flagged.  Handler would scatter treats on green turf as dog would pass by, would sniff treats but not eat them.  Walked towards water pool & started to sniff rocks while keeping tail flagged.  Handler would approach dog slowly, dog would pin ears back, keep tail flagged, become whale eyed & lick lips.  Handler went to reach for leash, dog would start to low growl then walk away as handler took a step back.  Handler was able to pick up leash, slowly attached a clip leash then walked to PY gate.  Slowly extended hand to pet on head prior to opening PY gate, dog would start to low growl again while lowering head, handler would removed hands & proceeded to walk out of PY.  Dog would attempt to fence fight while walking past reactive dogs in "D" building again, continued to use leash to help guide dog away from fences.  Would enter into kennel on own, removed leash with use of clip leash.
9/8/2026
Dog was at front of kennel; rounded body; lowered head; slowly crouched at front of kennel; tossed treats; dog remained at front; slowly closed divider; dog retreated to back of kennel; came back forward; attempted to place leash over head; flinched; tried again; leashed; dog exited; moderate to hard pull; startled by reactive dogs; pushed into middle buidling barrier; exited building; moderate pull; ears back; walked past kennels; pulled towards kennels; briefly fence fought; entered yard. In yard, dog explored; distant from handler; sniffing nose to ground; verbally coaxed; offered treats; not interested; urinated; defecated; interested in staff walking by; watched staff briefly; continued to explore; handler tried to slowly approach; dog would move away; sat in middle of yard; allowed handler to fully approach; tolerated petting; lowered head; allowed handler to swap leashes slowly due to first leash being soiled. Picked leash up; exited; hackles became raised when walking past kennels; entered building; tense body; pulled towards kennels; briefly fence fought; used light leash pressure; continued walking; entered kennel; allowed for leash removal.
9/5/2026
Dog did not eat vocal in back of kennel refused tossed treat.

stiff body, trembling, wide eyed, head low, allowed some petting, not seeking any attention, some hard stares a few times, allowed restraint vaccinations given, walked to kennel

What is the reason for surrender?
PER SOURCE, ASSISTED LIVING IS NOT THE BEST SITUATION FOR THIS DOG THAT HAS LIVED HIS ENTIRE LIFE UNTIL 11 MONTHS AGO IN A HOUSE WITH A LARGE YARD.  THE CONFINED SPACE WAS HARD ON THE DOG, THE AGING OWNER IS UNWELL AND IT WAS VERY HARD ON HER TO KEEP THE DOG AT THE FACILITY.  NO YARD AND THE MANAGER WAS NEVER PLEASED TO HAVE HIM THERE, THEY WERE CONFINED TO A BEDROOM UNLESS LEASHED TO GO OUT.

10+ YEARS

BREEDER. ATTEMPTED TO RETURN PET TO THE BREEDER, NO REPLY.

NEUTERED

HE HAS HAD VALLEY FEVER, TAKEN ANTI FUNGAL OFF AND ON FOR SEVERAL YEARS.  SKIN AILMENTS FROM ALLERGIES.
We offer resources such as low-cost veterinary care, trainers, food/medication coupons, and financial assistance. Would you like any resources instead of surrendering?
NO

NO, THE BITE BROKE THE SKIN.  JUST ONE BITE ON THE LOW ARM, WRIST AREA.

NO

AUGUST 31

NO, HE WILL GROWL A WARNING IF SOMETHING IS AMISS, BUT NOT AGGRESSIVE.
Has the animal ever seriously injured or caused the death of another animal?
NO

HE HAS BEEN AROUND CHILDREN OF ALL AGES (0-ADULT) AND WITH SUPERVISION AND RESPECT, HE LIKES KIDS.  HE SPENT AN EXTENDED STAY, MORE THAN 3 WEEKS WITH A PET SITTER AT HER HOUSE.  SHE HAS 2 DOGS AND 5 CHILDREN AGE 2-11.  A4060980 WARMED UP TO ALL BUT ONE OF THE DOGS.  AND THEY KEPT THEM SEPARATED.

CAUTIOUS AND THEN LOVING.  IT TAKES HIM TIME TO WARM UP TO ANYONE, AND IF GREETED RAPIDLY OR WITH ROUGH PLAY HE WILL RETREAT AND POSSIBLY GROWL.  IF GIVEN A PERIOD OF TIME TO COME TO SOMEONE AND WARM UP, HE WILL CHOOSE IF AND WHEN

70+ WOMAN, 80+ MAN.  GRANDCHILDREN INTERMITTENT 2-18

YES, IGNORES THEM

TAKES TIME TO WARM UP TO THEM

UNKNOWN

IGNORES THEM.  THERE WERE TORTOISES, A BIRD AND A CAT.  HE HAS BEEN AROUND MANY SMALL ANIMALS.

HE WAS THE ONLY DOG IN THE HOUSE, NO RESOURCE GUARDING

YES

YES

YES

YES

YES! VERY GOOD ON WALKS

BASIC SIT, STAY (SOMETIMES) BUT VERY SMART AND COULD LEARN MORE WITH TRAINING

INSIDE, WITH A DOG DOOR TO A LARGE YARD UNTIL THE OWNER WENT TO ASSISTED LIVING THEN NO YARD ONLY WALKS OUTSIDE ON A LEASH SEVERAL TIMES A DAY

After some time handlers were able to return dogs to taxi, dog was again able to be treat trailed into taxi and then Assistant handler was able to use leash removing device to free dog of initial leash wrapped around waist. Dog snapped at assistant handler a few times during removal. Handlers were able to hold leash taut and quickly place clip leashes behind dogs heads and transport back to kennel.
